Scalability

The ability to increase or decrease the computational resources required to execute a varying volume of tasks, processes, or services. Scalability allows systems to tackle more complex or larger scale problems effectively.1 This helps keep services fast and reliable, even when demand changes.

How it is used

A key application of scalability is in web applications. The County can scale up or down computing power for web applications based on the demand. Scalability is a key factor in capacity planning, ensuring that resources are available when needed while optimizing the cost of operation.
